does: Cooks small vegetables in a little water, butter and sugar until the water has gone and they are left tender and coated in a shiny syrup.

intro.what: This vegetable glaze reduces water, butter and sugar into a shiny coating around small vegetables.
intro.why: It connects tenderness with evaporation, so you can form a glaze without continuing to soften the vegetables too far.

how: Put the vegetables in a wide pan in a single layer.
Add water to come half way up them, with butter, a little sugar and salt.
Cover with a round of paper and simmer until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Take the paper off and boil away the last of the liquid, rolling the vegetables in the syrup as it forms.
Stop there for a pale glaze, or go on a moment for a golden one.

cues.text: No liquid is left: a shiny film coats each piece and the pan.
The bubbling turns to a sizzle as the last of the water goes.

mistakes.mistake: Too much water, so that the vegetables are overcooked before it has gone.
mistakes.fix: Use less, and pour some off if they are tender before the glaze forms.

mistakes.mistake: Walking away at the end, when the syrup burns.

quiz.question: What turns the cooking liquid into a glaze?
choices: Evaporating the water until a shiny syrup coats the vegetables.
Keeping plenty of watery liquid around them.
Adding flour to make an opaque sauce.
quiz.because: As water leaves, the remaining syrup becomes a shiny film around the pieces.

quiz.question: What do you do as the last liquid boils away?
choices: Leave them still against the pan.
Roll the vegetables in the forming syrup.
Cover them again to trap the steam.
quiz.because: Rolling coats the vegetables in the syrup as it forms and keeps you attending to the final stage.

quiz.question: What sound marks the last of the water leaving?
choices: A sizzle becomes a quiet simmer.
The pan stays full of gently bubbling water.
quiz.because: The sound shifts to a sizzle when little water remains and the glaze coats the pan.

quiz.question: The vegetables are tender but too much liquid remains. What would you do?
choices: Pour some liquid off rather than waiting for all of it to boil away.
Keep simmering until the vegetables break down.
Add more water to delay glazing.
quiz.because: Too much starting water can soften vegetables too far before the glaze forms.
